# Guarded cell -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** Run the transfer cell without ever writing belt.rotate. You command starter.coil; the contactor runs the motor. The safety relay watches one interlock contact from each leaf of the cell gate and holds your coil off until both leaves are shut and somebody presses Reset — so the relay closing hands the coil back and starts nothing. Cartons have to cross the scanner's protective field, so bridge it with scanner.mute while each one passes; the panel's pot is how long you bridge it for. Then transfer each carton into the chute with the cylinder, sequencing on the two reeds and never energising both coils.

**Done when.** Cartons reach transferred.count while your program has never written belt.rotate — belt.rotate follows starter.aux, because the contactor runs the motor and you only run the coil. Opening either gate leaf stops the cell inside 200 ms; closing both and pressing Reset lights relay.k1 and starts nothing at all, and Start is what starts it. Open one leaf on its own and, past the relay's sync window, relay.fault latches: a reset while it is still open will not clear it. Finally turn the pot past the scanner's own mute limit and watch scanner.muted go out while scanner.mute is still commanded — your mute stopped being a mute, the next carton in the field stopped the cell, and that is what a mute without a limit hides.

The Siemens walkthrough -- PLCSIM Advanced, the OPC UA server, finding
NodeIds -- is [`../README.md`](../README.md). This page is only what is
different about this scene.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `guarded_cell.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"GuardedCell"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"GuardedCell"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Guarded cell" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/guarded_cell.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU:

```bash
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/guarded-cell/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/guarded-cell/snap7_mapping.json
factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/guarded-cell/plcsim_mapping.json
```

(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`factoryforge-sidecar`, run from the repository root so the paths resolve.)
To have it marked, run `python tools/grade.py --scene guarded-cell` in place
of the 3D scene and add the `--port` it prints to the same command.

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 22 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cylinder.extend` | PLC writes | `CylinderExtend` | Bool | DBX0.0 | extend coil (5/2 valve, no spring: the rod stays where it was last driven) | yes |
| `cylinder.retract` | PLC writes | `CylinderRetract` | Bool | DBX0.1 | retract coil | yes |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | `EmitterEmit` | Bool | DBX0.2 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll | yes |
| `guard_a.lock` | PLC writes | `GuardALock` | Bool | DBX0.3 | energise the solenoid lock (it only bites on a shut door) |  |
| `guard_b.lock` | PLC writes | `GuardBLock` | Bool | DBX0.4 | energise the solenoid lock (it only bites on a shut door) |  |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX0.5 | green lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX0.6 | red lamp on the panel | yes |
| `relay.reset` | PLC writes | `RelayReset` | Bool | DBX0.7 | reset: the relay closes on a RISING edge, and only with both channels healthy | yes |
| `scanner.mute` | PLC writes | `ScannerMute` | Bool | DBX1.0 | request muting; honoured for at most 6 s at a stretch | yes |
| `starter.coil` | PLC writes | `StarterCoil` | Bool | DBX1.1 | contactor coil -- the contactor runs belt.rotate | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | `TowerGreen` | Bool | DBX1.2 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | `TowerRed` | Bool | DBX1.3 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | `TowerYellow` | Bool | DBX1.4 | tower lamp, yellow |  |
| `line_end.count` | PLC reads | `LineEndCount` | DInt | DBD2 | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total |  |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD6 | the operator's pot, 1..10 s (starts at 3.5) | yes |
| `starter.current` | PLC reads | `StarterCurrent` | Real | DBD10 | motor current, A | yes |
| `transferred.count` | PLC reads | `TransferredCount` | DInt | DBD14 | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |
| `belt.fault` | PLC reads | `BeltFault` | Bool | DBX18.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `cylinder.extended` | PLC reads | `CylinderExtended` | Bool | DBX18.1 | reed switch at full stroke | yes |
| `cylinder.fault` | PLC reads | `CylinderFault` | Bool | DBX18.2 | TRUE = the cylinder has seized |  |
| `cylinder.retracted` | PLC reads | `CylinderRetracted` | Bool | DBX18.3 | reed switch at home; mid-stroke neither reed is made | yes |
| `guard_a.closed` | PLC reads | `GuardAClosed` | Bool | DBX18.4 | guard switch, normally closed: TRUE while the door is shut | yes |
| `guard_a.locked` | PLC reads | `GuardALocked` | Bool | DBX18.5 | TRUE while the door is locked shut |  |
| `guard_b.closed` | PLC reads | `GuardBClosed` | Bool | DBX18.6 | guard switch, normally closed: TRUE while the door is shut | yes |
| `guard_b.locked` | PLC reads | `GuardBLocked` | Bool | DBX18.7 | TRUE while the door is locked shut |  |
| `mute_eye.detect` | PLC reads | `MuteEyeDetect` | Bool | DBX19.0 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX19.1 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX19.2 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX19.3 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX19.4 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `push_eye.detect` | PLC reads | `PushEyeDetect` | Bool | DBX19.5 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `relay.cha` | PLC reads | `RelayCha` | Bool | DBX19.6 | channel A as the relay sees it (guard_a.closed) |  |
| `relay.chb` | PLC reads | `RelayChb` | Bool | DBX19.7 | channel B as the relay sees it (guard_b.closed) |  |
| `relay.fault` | PLC reads | `RelayFault` | Bool | DBX20.0 | TRUE = the two channels disagreed; the relay latches this fault | yes |
| `relay.k1` | PLC reads | `RelayK1` | Bool | DBX20.1 | safety contact K1: TRUE while the relay's outputs are closed (open, they hold starter.coil FALSE) | yes |
| `relay.k2` | PLC reads | `RelayK2` | Bool | DBX20.2 | safety contact K2: TRUE while the relay's outputs are closed | yes |
| `scanner.muted` | PLC reads | `ScannerMuted` | Bool | DBX20.3 | TRUE while muting is actually in force | yes |
| `scanner.stop` | PLC reads | `ScannerStop` | Bool | DBX20.4 | protective field clear, normally closed: TRUE = clear, FALSE = someone is in it | yes |
| `scanner.warn` | PLC reads | `ScannerWarn` | Bool | DBX20.5 | TRUE while the warning field is broken | yes |
| `starter.aux` | PLC reads | `StarterAux` | Bool | DBX20.6 | auxiliary contact: TRUE while the contactor has really pulled in | yes |
| `starter.overload` | PLC reads | `StarterOverload` | Bool | DBX20.7 | thermal overload, normally closed: TRUE = OK, FALSE = tripped | yes |
| `belt.rotate` | PLC writes | -- | -- | -- | starter.coil's contactor drives it; a program that writes it fails this exercise |  |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.

## Not in FF_IO

`belt.rotate`: starter.coil's contactor drives it; a program that writes it fails this exercise. It has no member and no mapping, so
the sidecar reports it as unmapped -- which is correct.
